purpose: External eval set for vibe-agent-instructions. Prompts live outside skills/ so they are not bundled as skill content. Fixture-based evals deliver a represented target repository as a regular-file subtree under evals/vibe-agent-instructions/fixtures/ and name it as the target repository's root; behavior is judged from the change manifest (created, modified, and deleted paths and their types, including symlink; the manifest does not distinguish ignored from non-ignored additions, so ignore rules are proved from printed ignore-file content) together with the file contents and link targets each prompt requires the executor to print. Prompt-only evals are response-only, because the sandbox root is a copy of this repository and already carries its own AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. The suite exercises create mode with the reference-folder choice, update mode's observation binding with the commit handoff, the local-rules managed block and its repair, the derived-file link rule and its stub fallback, link-integrity classes for both derived files, the inventory with a pre-existing tracked root override, both conflict stops, the preview, placement, and divergence stops on separate consent channels, the divergence gate at a stale evidence date, a user's settled decision written as a decision record, and refusal to activate on an implicit mention.
coverage_notes: Coverage map: create mode, the read-when table, the maintenance line, reuse of an existing developer-docs folder, the size guard, the loader matrix, and the report sections -> E01; update mode's observation binding, the unverifiable human rule, the embedded directive, and the commit handoff -> E02; local-rules creation with the managed block, a named .gitignore placement, Codex's discretionary read, and the restart notice -> E03; the stub fallback as a prompt-stated premise -> E05; link integrity (CLAUDE.md link text and diverged copy, CLAUDE.local.md other content and exact stub) together with managed-block insertion and repair -> E06 (cases A, B); the inventory with a pre-existing tracked root override, the tracked-personal-file stop, and the ignored-derived-file stop -> E07; refusal to activate on an implicit mention -> E09; the preview stop, the placement stop, and the divergence stop, each on its own consent channel -> E10 (cases A, B, C; case C also carries report-and-ask at a current evidence date); the stale evidence date and the divergence content -> E13; a user's settled decision during an update, with a rejected alternative, written as a decision record under the durable-records duty -> E15. Common assertions: the preview reproduction and the source/derived pair naming. Observation paths: link creation is observed through the change manifest's symlink entries, expected on the Codex executor lane; a lane that cannot create links satisfies the same expectations through the documented stub with its concrete trigger named. File contents are observed through the executor's printed output, which is why every fixture prompt asks for it; whether generated files suit a real repository, and the actual absence of a commit, stay human-only (the manifest cannot distinguish a committed change from an uncommitted one, so E02 asserts only the response's history claims and commands). Fixture limits: every fixture path is tracked at the sandbox baseline; E07 relies on that for the tracked-personal-file stop, while E06 states in its prompt that its personal files are untracked and already Git-ignored. Fixtures cannot carry symbolic links, so pre-existing links are regular-file stand-ins (link text in materialized-link/CLAUDE.md, the exact stub in diverged-copy/CLAUDE.local.md), and find evals/vibe-agent-instructions/fixtures -type l must stay empty. Fixture instruction files hold only harmless sample rules about a fictional widget service, because an agent reading those directories may load them. Known uncovered: a policy-divergence acceptance or non-conforming repository written as a decision record, the no-shell degraded mode, the non-Git-directory limitation, the re-check of ignore rules on a chosen reference folder, the default docs/agents/ folder when no docs location exists, and the CLAUDE.md identical-copy and conforming-import and CLAUDE.local.md link-text classes, whose dispositions match classes E06 exercises.
common_assertions: For every already-existing path the run reports changing, the response shows the change itself: its diff, its complete new content, or, for a path replaced by a symbolic link, the path and the link target. An outcome sentence alone, a link to the file, or a statement that a preview was shown does not count. One block may cover several paths when it names each of them and their new content is identical. If the response reports writing only paths that did not exist before, or nothing, and the change manifest agrees (no modified, deleted, or replaced path), this assertion passes by non-applicability.

When the run writes, previews, classifies, or blocks a change to either member of an instruction-file pair, the report names both members and marks which one is the source: `AGENTS.md` with the derived `CLAUDE.md`, and `AGENTS.override.md` with the derived `CLAUDE.local.md`. Labelling one member the source or the other derived is enough. A pair the run does not act on is not required, and a pair reported only as absent is not acted on; naming one member of a pair the run did act on without its counterpart fails. If the response states that the skill is not activated and does no instruction-file work, this assertion passes by non-applicability.
